approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from accepted scored molecules. It samples breeding parents from high-scoring population quantiles, applies connected-fragment crossover or successive local atom and bond edits, and fills a fresh surplus pool after graph validation, stable canonical identity checks and duplicate rejection. Direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled. A Gaussian process fitted to the complete task-local accepted archive uses integer-count Morgan features and generalized Tanimoto similarity. Correlated function draws choose distinct pool members for evaluation; real accepted scores then update the archive and a bounded score-greedy population.
approach.novelty: Remove the composite posterior selector's influence on successful emissions: take the first announced batch of valid unique pool members in generation order. Keep the complete inherited pool, model fitting, full covariance and original draws as passive controls. Earlier siblings removed counts, sampled residuals or their correlation while retaining predictive allocation. This test instead removes all predictive ranking at once at the existing pool boundary, treating the selector as one module. The independent sampled comparator records which identities would differ on each actual pool; it supplies no scores for unevaluated alternatives.

hypothesis: Remove all posterior-based influence on successful offspring allocation by selecting the first announced-batch-size valid unique candidates in inherited generation order from the fully generated pool, while retaining the complete accepted-only posterior computation and original draws passively.

finding_summary.headline: Generation-order allocation loses 0.124388 in mean endpoint score despite retaining full pool and model effort.
finding_summary.insights:
This closes a different question from the earlier count, residual and correlation controls: allocating evaluations using the complete predictive selector matters even when generation effort is held at the inherited full-pool boundary. The earlier selector addition also enlarged the pool and lacked a complete matched Parent panel, so it could not establish this conditional contrast. Local parent beats increased from 629 to 653, yet incumbent improvements fell from 258 to 163; adaptive local success is not a substitute for endpoint quality. The present loss does not apportion value among posterior means, counts, residual amplitude or correlation, and separate sibling losses cannot be added.

A plausible place to investigate the loss is how evaluation choices preserve useful chemical relationships across adaptive histories. The molecular report finds that generation-order output still reaches useful nitrile and aryl-amine alternatives, including both improved endpoints, while other streams move into densely connected heteroatom frameworks and miss strong Parent families. Reactive bonds, questionable ring geometry and unspecified stereochemistry persist. This concerns the evaluated distribution; it does not show that better alternatives were absent from the complete pools or identify a chemical mediator. Passive alternatives have no counterfactual scores.

Removing predictive influence is also different from removing computational cost: all surplus generation and model computations remain, and numerical failures would still use the inherited routes. No reduced-pool, compute-saving or optimizer-deletion conclusion follows. Actual recovery branches remain unexercised despite passing deterministic synthetic checks.
finding_summary.results:
All 435 successful batches evaluated the first ten members of a completed 160-member pool, with zero prefix-order violations or choices outside that prefix. The passive original sampler selected a different set in all 435 batches, and its sampled values strictly preferred another candidate on 4,317 of 4,350 generation-order masks. Thus the removal changed real evaluation choices under strong exposure. All 435 fits, full covariance factorizations and original normal arrays remained computed; the accepted-only feedback and identity-bound prediction joins passed. No natural numerical fallback or incomplete pool occurred.

Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.595670 to 0.471282, a paired change of -0.124388, well beyond the registered 0.002 loss scale. Seed macro changes were -0.134968, -0.105769 and -0.132426. All five task means declined. Thirteen of fifteen task-seed endpoints declined; zaleplon_mpo seeds zero and one improved by 0.019694 and 0.005802. Macro population deviation changed from 0.026593 to 0.014583. Correct removal and the predicted score loss support positive contribution from the composite selector in this exact full-pool search loop.

molecular.headline: Aromatic families remain, with useful nitrile and aryl-amine alternatives alongside peroxides, O-halogen bonds and difficult rings
molecular.overall_character: All supplied Child n-01b48dd09404 and published Parent n-62daf219c70a trajectories were read, with no missing paths or uncovered objectives. The brief reports child_complete=true and paired_complete=true for Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2, with no profile mismatches. Each task has 900 Child trajectory records, including 870 optimizer records, and a complete matched Parent panel. The fixed initial molecules and their scores match within each paired task/seed. These trajectories describe accepted evaluated molecules; they do not enumerate every valid pool member, unselected candidate or rejected graph. The digest field proposed_by_optimizer and all chemistry frequencies below therefore concern recorded optimizer evaluations, not a census of the complete inherited generation pool. An emitted molecule, an accepted evaluation, and the highest observed retained endpoint are different observations. The digest final_molecules are late seed-2 evaluations, not every seed's retained incumbent; full trajectories supply the endpoint comparisons. The registered contrast removes posterior influence on successful allocation at full inherited pool effort while retaining posterior computation passively. This report does not audit activation, describe deletion of the optimizer, attribute chemistry to an individual posterior component, or infer pool reduction or compute savings. The output contains indole amides and ketones, nitrile-bearing biaryl amines attached to unsaturated ether/peroxide rings, linked aza-aromatic carbonyl systems, aryl tertiary amines, fused nitrogen diones, and both fluorinated aza-aromatics and densely oxygenated nonaromatic cages. Child ring-closure-string incidences are 0.9598, 0.9724, 0.9805, 0.9448 and 0.9437 in fixed task order; aromatic-string incidences are 0.9506, 0.9701, 0.9563, 0.9402 and 0.6609. These measure feature presence in molecular strings, not perceived ring counts or aromatic-atom fractions. The final stream includes a wholly nonaromatic seed family, so aromatic richness is not universal within every seed. Formal-charge and stereocentre-string incidences are 0.0 throughout. Available aliphatic amines and potentially stereogenic centres remain plainly present. Read-only RDKit perception of the exact trajectory graphs supports size, ring and functional-group descriptions; no new objective, affinity, feasibility or synthesis scores were calculated. The overall chemistry remains questionable in synthetic plausibility and weak in drug-likeness, with ordinary medicinal functional groups mixed with O-F/O-Cl bonds, peroxides, acyl fluoride, unusual carbon-sulfur triple bonds, strained unsaturation and unspecified stereochemistry. The relatively conventional tertiary-amine ketone and successful carbonyl-free nitrile family are important counterexamples: neither reactive bonds nor the Parent's exact scaffold families are universal necessities. Across-seed structural diversity is moderate, with narrower related series among each seed's leaders. No general absence of rings, amines or scaffold alternatives is demonstrated, especially in the unobserved pool. The original n-c55c3d520a2c report and its carry-forward in n-62daf219c70a were read through the fresh evidence index. The transferable gaps retain that provenance and are re-observed here under the current complete matched conditions; historical origin is not extra replication. Only Child SMILES from the digest or the trusted citation_trajectory_paths are quoted. Parent-only structures are described by published task/seed/evaluation. Read-only evidence and descriptors are in .slots/r0017-02-ablation-L01/molecular/trajectory_audit.json and inspected_records.json; history_molecular_sources.json preserves the original reports and source hashes. No structural association below assigns a reward to an unselected pool molecule or establishes which chemical change mediated the endpoint contrast.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-1 leader (evaluation 203) is a compact nitrile-bearing phenyl/pyridyl system connected through an NH group to an unsaturated oxygen ring containing an O-O bond and a fluoroethyl side chain. Related high-scoring members instead have a cyclic ether without peroxide. This family contains no carbonyl and no N-halogen bond. Seed 0 reaches a fused/bridged indole carboxanilide with methoxy, methyl and ordinary aryl fluorine substitution; seed 2 reaches an indole-linked aryl ketone with an additional O-CH2-N-containing ring. These leading molecules are compact, ring-rich and substantially aromatic. Mean Child SMILES length is 45.4, with a maximum of 95 and halogen-string incidence of 0.7609. The Parent leaders are an amino-substituted cumulene on an N-chloro indole (seed 0, evaluation 289), an N-hydroxy pyridyl amide with N-F (seed 1, 293), and an N-chloro indole vicinal diketone (seed 2, 294). The Child reaches higher retained endpoints in seeds 0 and 1 and a lower endpoint in seed 2, while avoiding N-halogen bonds in all these cited Child leaders. That is heterogeneous chemical change, not a uniform loss of useful chemistry.
liabilities: The seed-1 leader contains an O-O bond in an unsaturated ring. Its supplied score does not demonstrate stability or make the peroxide necessary; a cyclic ether relative also scores highly.

The other leaders have unusual fused/bridged connectivity or an O-CH2-N local environment and no stereochemical specification. Their conventional amide, ketone and aryl fluorine groups do not certify a route for the entire graph.
Very small fragments and much larger joined structures can both have negligible scores; molecular size is not a sufficient chemical quality rule.
missing_features: Consistent conventional alternatives preserving the favorable aromatic/polar organization are not established throughout the evaluated stream; the nonperoxide cyclic ether is already accessible and useful, so peroxide chemistry is not an unavoidable limitation.
Defined stereochemistry and conformational identity are absent for the fused/bridged saturated centres, while the unsaturated peroxide ring requires a distinct stability assessment.

The trajectory does not reveal an exact absent target pharmacophore. Both carbonyl-bearing and carbonyl-free leading frameworks exist, so the missing capability is reliable feasible alternatives rather than a prescribed carbonyl motif.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The general concern originates in n-c55c3d520a2c and was carried by n-62daf219c70a. method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

finding_summary.insights:
This closes a different question from the earlier count, residual and correlation controls: allocating evaluations using the complete predictive selector matters even when generation effort is held at the inherited full-pool boundary. The earlier selector addition also enlarged the pool and lacked a complete matched Parent panel, so it could not establish this conditional contrast. Local parent beats increased from 629 to 653, yet incumbent improvements fell from 258 to 163; adaptive local success is not a substitute for endpoint quality. The present loss does not apportion value among posterior means, counts, residual amplitude or correlation, and separate sibling losses cannot be added.

A plausible place to investigate the loss is how evaluation choices preserve useful chemical relationships across adaptive histories. The molecular report finds that generation-order output still reaches useful nitrile and aryl-amine alternatives, including both improved endpoints, while other streams move into densely connected heteroatom frameworks and miss strong Parent families. Reactive bonds, questionable ring geometry and unspecified stereochemistry persist. This concerns the evaluated distribution; it does not show that better alternatives were absent from the complete pools or identify a chemical mediator. Passive alternatives have no counterfactual scores.

Removing predictive influence is also different from removing computational cost: all surplus generation and model computations remain, and numerical failures would still use the inherited routes. No reduced-pool, compute-saving or optimizer-deletion conclusion follows. Actual recovery branches remain unexercised despite passing deterministic synthetic checks.

finding_summary.insights:
This closes a different question from the earlier count, residual and correlation controls: allocating evaluations using the complete predictive selector matters even when generation effort is held at the inherited full-pool boundary. The earlier selector addition also enlarged the pool and lacked a complete matched Parent panel, so it could not establish this conditional contrast. Local parent beats increased from 629 to 653, yet incumbent improvements fell from 258 to 163; adaptive local success is not a substitute for endpoint quality. The present loss does not apportion value among posterior means, counts, residual amplitude or correlation, and separate sibling losses cannot be added.

A plausible place to investigate the loss is how evaluation choices preserve useful chemical relationships across adaptive histories. The molecular report finds that generation-order output still reaches useful nitrile and aryl-amine alternatives, including both improved endpoints, while other streams move into densely connected heteroatom frameworks and miss strong Parent families. Reactive bonds, questionable ring geometry and unspecified stereochemistry persist. This concerns the evaluated distribution; it does not show that better alternatives were absent from the complete pools or identify a chemical mediator. Passive alternatives have no counterfactual scores.

Removing predictive influence is also different from removing computational cost: all surplus generation and model computations remain, and numerical failures would still use the inherited routes. No reduced-pool, compute-saving or optimizer-deletion conclusion follows. Actual recovery branches remain unexercised despite passing deterministic synthetic checks.
